{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development, Hosting and Revenue-Share Agreement with HDI)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for the Company / Customer)  
**Basis:** Verified playbook findings only. Section references below are taken from the findings; the two anchors "§ 1.4" and "§ 5.4" are the document locations recorded for our proposed insertions/redlines.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings: 3 critical, 5 high, 9 medium, 1 low**. Four provisions are compliant (governing law, MFN, minimum commitments, and the absence of an employee non-solicit — the last requiring an internal verification pass), and the balance require action.

The dominant theme is **absence of core risk allocation**. The Agreement contains **no indemnification, no IP ownership provision, no limitation of liability, no post-termination transition/data-return obligation, no performance warranty and no insurance covenant**. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site, holds our Content, our Marks, export/order files and user information (Sections 1.3, 1.5, 2.1, 8.1), yet nothing states who owns the Site, the deliverables or our customer and order data, and nothing obliges HDI to perform in a workmanlike manner, to hand our data back, or to carry insurance. Section 9 is limited to corporate authority representations plus a Globix acknowledgement; Section 10 contains no liability terms.

The second theme is **asymmetric exit and lock-in economics**. Section 4.1 gives either party a 90-day convenience exit off a one-year auto-renewing term, but Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment on the Company alone — 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — which on the finding can substantially exceed a full year of fees (fees are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month under Section 3.1) and is not disapplied where we terminate for HDI's default. Section 6.1 then locks us out of any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products for the whole (indefinitely renewing) term, with no performance-based release. Section 3.4 gives HDI an inspection right over our records with **no frequency limit at all**.

Mitigants worth noting: HDI's reciprocal two-year non-compete in Section 6.3 benefits us and is untouched; Section 10.5 selects New York law (our preferred position); there is no MFN, no minimum volume commitment, no change-of-control trigger and no disclaimer of implied warranties; Section 4.2(b)/(c) floor the Termination Payment at zero and allow eight quarterly instalments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section / anchor | Position and action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion anchor); no indemnity anywhere; Sections 9, 10 | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless anywhere; the only infringement reference is a mutual advertising covenant. Walk-away territory. Insert HDI indemnity as new Section 9(c) (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-supplied Content/Marks. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 (insertion anchor); Sections 5.2, 8, 10.2 | No ownership clause. We supply all Content and license the "Deerskin" Marks; HDI builds and hosts the Site and collects customer/order data. Section 5.2 gives us artistic/editorial control only. Insert new Section 5.5: we retain Content, Marks and customer/order data; HDI assigns Site/deliverables with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for its pre-existing platform; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion anchor); Sections 9, 10 | No cap, exclusion or aggregate-liability language. Insert new Section 10.9: mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; uncapped carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); Sections 3 and 4.2 payments are not "damages". Fallback: straight twelve-month fee cap. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4; Section 4.2(a) (with 4.2(b)/(c)) | Company-only Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 can exceed a year of fees and is not disapplied on HDI default. Fails preferred and fallback. Proposed fallback: cap at three months' fees and disapply where we terminate for HDI's breach. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4; Sections 4.1, 4.2(a), 1.6, 3.1 | The 90-day mutual notice mechanics sit at the fallback and are not redlined. The defect is the one-sided Termination Payment. Cap at three months' Section 3.1 fees and disapply for termination on HDI's breach or under the Section 1.6 launch-failure right. No prepaid fees to refund (monthly in arrears). |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4; Sections 6.1, 4.1, 4.2(a), 1.6, 6.3 | Term-long exclusivity on the Company over Deerskin Products and substantially similar products, made open-ended by annual auto-renewal, with no performance-based release. Close to walk-away territory. Proposed fallback: narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months from the Effective Date, automatic release on HDI launch or performance failure. HDI's reciprocal Section 6.3 covenant left untouched. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4; Sections 6.1, 6.2, 1.1, 4.1, 6.3 | Section 6.1 reaches "substantially similar" products and an open-ended class of third-party products, with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out (only closeouts and the Joan Cook Catalog), and runs indefinitely via auto-renewal. Term-only (no post-term tail), so not walk-away. Proposed fallback: Deerskin Products only, 12-month cap, internal-development/acquisition carve-out. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4; Section 10.3 | Section 10.3 is successors/no-third-party-beneficiary only. No restriction on our assignment and no change-of-control trigger (good), but HDI may assign freely, including to a competitor, with no notice or consent — fails the fallback. Add affiliate/successor right for us, confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right, and a consent/no-competitor gate on HDI assignment. Fallback: mutual successor assignment on notice with reasonable-consent standard. |
| 9 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insertion anchor); Sections 4, 1.3, 1.5, 2.1, 8.1, 10.7 | No exit obligations: no migration assistance, no return/export of our Content, order files or user information, no deletion timetable; Section 10.7 survival covers only 6.3, 7, 9 and 10. Falls short of even the fallback. Insert new Section 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days (including Site credentials), certified deletion thereafter. |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4; Sections 9, 1.6, 5.2 | Section 9 is corporate reps plus the Globix acknowledgement only — no workmanlike-services, specification-conformance, legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. No implied-warranty disclaimer, so not walk-away. Insert new Section 9(c): workmanlike services, 12-month Site conformance, legal compliance, no malicious code, with repair/re-perform/refund. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4; Section 3.4 | Section 3.4 exceeds the playbook on notice (30 days), timing, cost (HDI bears fees) and no system access, but has **no frequency limit**, and unlimited audits are walk-away territory. Minimal edit: once per twelve months. Noted only: inspection by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor. |
| 12 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4; Sections 1.4, 6.1, 10.3 | The inbound grant (access to HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools) names only "the Company" — no extension to affiliates or contractors and no mechanism to add them; fails the fallback. Successor transfer is covered by Section 10.3 and there is no revocability-at-will language. Extend Section 1.4 rights to affiliates and contractors and confirm non-revocability during the term. Our outbound Marks licence in Section 6.1 benefits us and is not flagged. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4; Section 4.1 | One-year auto-renewal matches preferred, but the 90-day non-renewal notice window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Propose 30 days; 60 days acceptable. Noted only: no HDI renewal reminder, and no repricing/uplift language at all (so no CPI/3% cap needed). |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4; Section 10.5 | New York law is our preferred position; no arbitration clause and no off-list venue. Noted only: no express exclusive-jurisdiction reference to the state and federal courts in New York County — optional cleanup, not redlined. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4; Section 3 | No MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction; economics are a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold. Meets preferred position; no redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4; Sections 3, 4.1 | No minimum purchase, guaranteed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty, and no usage caps; revenue share only on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month. The Section 4.2 Termination Payment is an exit fee handled under LD/T4C; Section 6.1 is handled under the exclusivity/non-compete rules. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification: fail) | § 5.4; Sections 5.4, 10.2, 6, 6.3 | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement covenant binding the Company; Section 5.4 is a General Manager liaison provision and Section 10.2 disclaims employment/agency. Absence resolves to compliant on the analysis, with duration and carve-out checks inapplicable. **Verification did not pass — requires internal confirmation before we rely on it.** No redline or counterparty comment proposed; document text unchanged. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion anchor); Section 10 (10.1–10.8 subject matter) | No insurance covenant anywhere. HDI develops and hosts the Site and accesses Content, user information and other Company Confidential Information (Section 8.1); an uninsured hosting/data vendor is walk-away territory. Insert new Section 10.9: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

> Drafting note: both the limitation of liability and the insurance covenant are proposed as "new Section 10.9". These will need to be renumbered as 10.9 and 10.10 in the outgoing markup.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory (or immediately adjacent) and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No vendor indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** No IP indemnity for the Site HDI develops and hosts, and no coverage for HDI's breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Expressly recorded as walk-away territory.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE, low severity, walk-away characterisation).** Leaving a hosting vendor with access to our Content and user information uninsured is walk-away territory under the rule, notwithstanding the low severity rating.
3. **Unlimited vendor audit right (AUDIT, medium).** Section 3.4 has no frequency cap; unlimited audits are walk-away territory. The once-per-twelve-months cap is a minimal, non-negotiable fix.
4. **Company exclusivity in Section 6.1 (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** Assessed as close to walk-away territory: open-ended through auto-renewal, broad product scope, and no release for HDI's failure to keep the Site operational.

For completeness, the following are **not** in walk-away territory on the findings: the non-compete (term-only, no post-term tail), the renewal notice window (90 days is at, not above, the threshold), IP ownership (no assignment of our IP and no joint ownership), the performance warranty (no implied-warranty disclaimer), and assignment (no restriction on our assignment and no change-of-control trigger).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the markup** covering the three critical insertions (indemnity as Section 9(c); ownership as Section 5.5; limitation of liability as Section 10.9) plus insurance and the transition/data-return provision as Section 4.3. Renumber the two proposed 10.9 paragraphs.
2. **Open the commercial negotiation on exit economics as a single package**: cap the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment at three months' fees and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under the Section 1.6 launch-failure right. This is one commercial ask surfacing under both LD and T4C; the 90-day notice mechanics themselves are accepted.
3. **Negotiate the restrictive covenants as a paired ask**: narrow Section 6.1 to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months, add an automatic release on HDI performance failure and an internal-development/acquisition carve-out. Confirm internally that we are content to leave HDI's Section 6.3 covenant untouched as consideration.
4. **Send the low-friction fixes** likely to close quickly: the once-per-twelve-months audit cap (Section 3.4), extension of the Section 1.4 grant to affiliates and contractors, the assignment gate in Section 10.3, and the 30-day (fallback 60-day) non-renewal notice.
5. **Resolve the NOSOLICIT finding internally.** Verification failed on that item; confirm the absence of any employee non-solicit before we treat it as compliant. No counterparty comment until confirmed.
6. **Optional cleanup only if the document is otherwise reopening:** add an express exclusive-jurisdiction reference to the state and federal courts in New York County to Section 10.5. We would not reopen the agreement for this alone.
7. **Confirm fallback authority** with the business ahead of the call: twelve-month fee cap in lieu of the greater-of formulation; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M; 90-day warranty; 60-day non-renewal notice; and mutual successor assignment on notice with a reasonable-consent standard."}
